                    ### Question
                    A thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus strain has been isolated at a retirement home. Many of the elderly had been infected with this strain and are experiencing shingles. Which of the following would be the best antiviral agent to treat this population?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Acyclovir
opb. Famciclovir
opc. Ganciclovir
opd. Cidofovir
ope. Amantadine

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In the case of a thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus (VZV) strain, antiviral agents that require thymidine kinase for activation, such as Acyclovir, Famciclovir, and Ganciclovir, are ineffective. This is because these drugs rely on the viral thymidine kinase to convert them into their active forms. Cidofovir, however, does not require thymidine kinase for activation and can be effective against thymidine kinase-deficient VZV strains. Amantadine is not relevant as it targets influenza viruses, not VZV. Therefore, Cidofovir is the best antiviral agent to treat this population. The evidence path indicating that Cidofovir is effective without the need for thymidine kinase supports this conclusion.
